commands.author: MonkeyLeeT

target.title: fix(groq): keep default Llama agent turns within TPM limit
target.body:
Closes #104783

AI-assisted with Codex. I reviewed the implementation and the live proof.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running a local agent with `groq/llama-3.3-70b-versatile` could receive an immediate HTTP 413 for even a one-word prompt on Groq's 12,000 TPM base tier. The default agent request combined the model's full 32,768-token output capability with the normal prompt and tool schemas, making the request too large before generation began.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Groq plugin leaves the normal first request unchanged. Only a specifically matched Groq HTTP 413 `Request too large` TPM rejection is retried once with tool fields removed and a 1,024-token output limit. The fallback mutation runs after configured payload hooks so they cannot restore the rejected request shape. Explicit max-token overrides skip this recovery policy. Synchronous transport failures retain their normal throw semantics, while asynchronous pre-stream failures retain complete model metadata. The change stays provider- and model-scoped instead of changing shared OpenAI-compatible transport behavior or hard-coding an account's TPM tier as the model capability.

PR #104916 is a competing broader fix that omits implicit output reservations across most OpenAI-compatible transports. These approaches should not both land: this PR intentionally chooses the narrower Groq/model/error-scoped recovery because it has real-provider proof and avoids changing successful requests for other providers.

## User Impact

Default local-agent turns with `groq/llama-3.3-70b-versatile` can recover on Groq's base tier instead of failing immediately. Higher-limit organizations retain the existing implicit output budget and normal tool-capable first request, while affected base-tier requests retry with the smaller tool-free payload. Other Groq models and explicitly budgeted requests are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Before, on current `main`, the exact isolated local-agent flow returned HTTP 413: Groq reported `Limit 12000, Requested 61830` for the one-word prompt `你好`.
- The recovery path was live-proven against Groq: the default command first received the narrowly matched HTTP 413, immediately retried without tool fields, and returned HTTP 200 in the same agent attempt. Groq reported 10,071 input tokens and 452 output tokens (10,523 total).
- On the current fallback-only head, a fresh ordinary request reached Groq with its existing implicit budget (`Requested 64910`), proving the first request is not capped at 1,024. Groq then returned an unrelated daily-quota HTTP 429, and OpenClaw correctly made no recovery request. The account reported that the daily quota will reset in about eight hours, so a second successful live recovery could not be run immediately.
- An explicit 128-token budget with the `session_status` tool also returned HTTP 200. Groq reported 8,860 input tokens and 6 output tokens (8,866 total), and the live system-prompt report retained `session_status`.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/groq` — 5 tests passed, including a successful ordinary first request retaining `max_completion_tokens: 32768` and tools, a matching 413 retry canonicalized to only `max_completion_tokens: 1024` when an existing hook tries to restore either or both token aliases plus tools, configured and request-scoped explicit-budget preservation, non-recovery for unrelated 400/401/413-context/429 errors, synchronous throw preservation, and complete asynchronous error metadata.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/groq/index.test.ts` — clean.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/extensions-test.tsbuildinfo` — clean.
- `node scripts/check-extension-package-tsc-boundary.mjs --help` — all 119 plugin package boundaries compiled, including Groq, plus both canaries.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check extensions/groq/index.ts extensions/groq/index.test.ts` — clean.
- `git diff --check` — clean.

Hosted local validation was unavailable on this machine: Blacksmith Testbox was not installed, and direct AWS Crabbox had no usable instance credentials. The focused local fallback and live provider proof above completed successfully; GitHub CI remains the broad validation gate.
